summary: Pair each review image with exact application state, asset and software identities, capture settings and per-file digests so reviewers can reproduce the intended view and distinguish byte identity from visual approval.
objective: A reviewer can reconstruct every named capture state, verify package bytes, and identify which visual differences remain outside the manifest’s determinism boundary.
example_prompts: Package named product review views with their exact camera and toggle state.
Create a scene-review bundle whose screenshots can be traced to asset hashes.
Explain why matching archive hashes do not prove visual correctness.
not_for: Final time-sequence delivery already covered by frame-indexed animation export.
Treating a digest match as proof that an image is correct.

principles: A capture is a state record plus derived pixels. Store camera projection/world transform, scene time, selected IDs, visibility/layer state, material variants, environment, exposure/output transform, viewport CSS size, drawing-buffer size, pixel ratio and software/backend identity.

Determinism has a declared boundary. Exact bytes may vary with encoder, browser, renderer, GPU or driver even when the intended view matches; choose byte equality or a stated comparison method only after fixing the relevant inputs.
A digest identifies bytes, not meaning. Hash every manifest-listed file after serialization, but keep visual/domain review as a separate recorded result.
implementation: Freeze authoritative scene state before capture and use named cameras or explicit matrices rather than the reviewer’s current orbit. Wait only on declared asset/readiness barriers; record any temporal history reset required by the renderer.

Capture an origin-clean, non-zero-size canvas through toBlob with an explicit supported media type, await its callback, and reject a null Blob; alternatively use a backend-specific readback path whose color, alpha and orientation conversion is documented. Treat SecurityError, zero-size input, null serialization and unsupported readiness as explicit package failures rather than blank-image fallbacks.

Write a versioned manifest containing capture ID, semantic purpose, state, asset hashes, app commit/build, Three.js revision, renderer/backend, browser/OS where relevant, viewport/drawing-buffer sizes, color/output settings, file names and digest algorithm. Hash the actual serialized files and include a verification table.

Keep the package immutable. A reviewer records visual acceptance, tolerance and annotations alongside the capture identity; changing an image, manifest or annotation creates a new package revision rather than overwriting evidence.
observable_checks: Replaying each manifest state selects the same stable IDs and reproduces the declared camera, time, visibility and output settings before any pixel comparison.
Changing one image byte fails its file digest; restoring it passes. A passing digest is reported only as byte identity and never auto-marks visual review accepted.
A cross-origin asset that makes the canvas non-origin-clean, a zero-size canvas, or a null toBlob result causes an explicit failed capture with the responsible state or dependency identified.
Two supported encoders or backends may produce different bytes; the report applies the declared visual comparison boundary and retains both environment identities.

creative_affordances: The package may use contact sheets, paired before/after views, sectional plates or annotated hero shots.
Review annotations can be spatial overlays or external prose as long as their source capture stays identifiable.
known_limits: This profile does not guarantee cross-machine byte-identical pixels.
Web Crypto digest consumes the supplied bytes as one input; package tooling may choose another reviewed streaming hash implementation for large archives.
No screenshot, readback, digest, replay or visual comparison was run.

claims.statement: The HTML Standard defines canvas.toBlob as creating an image-file Blob, defaulting to PNG when the requested type is unsupported, and requires a SecurityError when the canvas bitmap is not origin-clean.
claims.scope: WHATWG HTML living standard canvas serialization read 2026-09-08; exact encoded bytes and supported optional formats remain user-agent dependent.

claims.statement: Web Cryptography Level 2 defines SubtleCrypto.digest as copying the supplied bytes, applying the normalized digest algorithm and resolving a Promise with an ArrayBuffer containing the digest.
claims.scope: W3C Web Cryptography Level 2 First Public Working Draft dated 2025-04-22, read 2026-09-08; a digest establishes equality of the hashed byte sequence, not visual or semantic correctness.
